book.title: The Telegraph All New Toughie Crossword, book 1

clue.text: Drunk with two men who had been taken along the way

definitions.text: had been taken along the way

blocks.note: high is slang for intoxicated
two men's names, Jack and Ed, placed side by side

explanation.surface: A drunk and two companions picked up by someone on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: HIGHJACKED is an older spelling of hijacked, which fits the 'along the way' hint at the highway. The two men are Jack and Ed.
explanation.definitionFit: A hijacked vehicle has been seized in transit, so it was taken while on the road.

clue.text: Draughty blow?

blocks.note: surface reading: a gust of air through a chilly room
setter's reading: in the game of draughts, a move that takes an opponent's piece as a penalty, which is also a puff of breath

explanation.walkthrough: Draughts is the British name for checkers. Removing a piece whose player failed to make a capture has its own name in that game, the same word as a puff of breath.
explanation.definitionFit: To huff is both to blow out air and, in checkers, to remove an opponent's piece as a forfeit.

clue.text: Garry and co. vandalised vehicle

indicators.note: vandalised things are smashed up, so the letters are broken and put back differently

blocks.note: the name plus the abbreviation for company; 'and' joins them

explanation.surface: A man called Garry and his friends wrecked a car.
explanation.walkthrough: CO is the abbreviation for company. A gyrocar is a two-wheeled car kept upright by a gyroscope.
explanation.definitionFit: A gyrocar is a motor car balanced on two wheels by a spinning gyroscope, so a kind of transport.

clue.text: Some hot stuff from the West Indies

definitions.text: Some hot stuff from the West Indies

blocks.note: surface reading: something fiery or exciting, perhaps a dance or a person
setter's reading: a pungent spice named after a Caribbean island

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot stuff' suggests something sexy or thrilling; it means spicy. The spice is the allspice berry, named after a Caribbean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Jamaica pepper is another name for allspice, the dried berry of a Caribbean tree used as a pungent seasoning.

clue.text: Kinsmen turn up during rocky ascent

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning something up makes it read from the bottom, so the word runs backwards
rocky means unsteady and shaken, so the letters of the next word are jumbled
during means in the middle of, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: a turn in a game is a go
used letter for letter

explanation.surface: Relatives make an appearance part-way through a difficult climb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn up' reads as arriving; it is a turn, a GO, written upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognates are relatives by blood, especially through the mother's line, so they are kin.

clue.text: Mother left mealies cooked for another lady ...

indicators.note: left means went away, so the word for mother goes from the letters
cooking transforms ingredients, so the remaining letters are mixed

blocks.note: ma is an informal word for mother
used letter for letter

explanation.surface: Mum went off and cooked maize for some other woman.
explanation.walkthrough: MA leaves MEALIES, giving ELIES, which is then rearranged. Mealies is southern African English for maize. The dots link to 7 Down, the next lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsie is a woman's first name, so it names a lady, one of a run of ladies in the puzzle.

clue.text: The man before a meal had a good deal

definitions.note: a noun phrase; 'had' is the link

blocks.note: the man is referred to as he
taken as written
the setter's route from meal to this single letter is unclear

explanation.surface: Someone got a bargain just before sitting down to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: HE and A account for three letters; how 'meal' gives the final P is not clear, and the crossing with 8 Down fixes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaps or a heap is informal for a large quantity, the same as saying a good deal.

clue.text: Lady in the clutches of one lean Oriental

indicators.note: something in the clutches of another is held inside it, so the run of words grips the target

blocks.note: the letters run across all three words

explanation.surface: A woman held captive by a thin man from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan has lost the first letter of 'Lady'. The answer is hidden across the last three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleanor is a woman's first name, so it names a lady, following the lady at 5 Down.

clue.text: Gently puppy and mole ruin bloomer

indicators.note: to ruin something is to wreck it, so the letters before it are broken up and rebuilt

blocks.note: p, for piano, is the musical direction to play softly
the two words used letter for letter; 'and' joins them

explanation.surface: A young dog and a mole gently wreck a gardener's flower bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests a blunder or a loaf of bread; here it is something that flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: The plume poppy, Macleaya, is a tall garden perennial with feathery flower heads, so a flowering plant.

clue.text: Meeting curious flying officer first

indicators.note: first says the officer's abbreviation goes at the front, before the odd word

blocks.note: FO is the RAF abbreviation for flying officer
rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A get-together with an odd air-force officer arriving before everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curious' looks like an anagram signal, but it is the word RUM, meaning strange.
explanation.definitionFit: A forum is an assembly or gathering held for public discussion.

clue.text: Alewife, one breathing water!

blocks.note: someone who gasps is breathing hard
eau is French for water

explanation.surface: A landlady who drinks water, which for a pub keeper is a surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: An alewife sounds like a woman who keeps an alehouse, but here it is the North American herring-like fish, called GASPEREAU in Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaspereau is the Canadian name for the alewife, a fish of the herring family.

clue.text: Mayflies repeat hop with mere abandon

indicators.note: doing something with abandon means wildly and without restraint, so the letters are thrown about

blocks.note: used letter for letter
used letter for letter

explanation.surface: Mayflies hop again and again over a lake, wildly.
explanation.walkthrough: A mere is a small lake, which fits the insects' habitat but serves only as letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemeroptera is the scientific order containing the mayflies, named for their very short adult lives.

clue.text: Game, technical version's effect on weather

indicators.note: a version is a reworked form of something, so the two words are rearranged

blocks.note: both words used letter for letter

explanation.surface: A technical form of some sport turns out to change the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' and 'technical' look like a sport's formal name; their letters are the fodder, and the possessive 's joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Climate change is a long-term shift in weather patterns, the broad effect felt on weather.

clue.text: Radical junior in charge of sound waves

definitions.note: a noun phrase standing for the adjective, as in ultrasonic waves

blocks.note: an ultra is an extremist
a junior is a son named after his father
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A young extremist runs the sound department.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: ULTRASONIC describes sound waves above the range of hearing rather than meaning them.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultrasonic waves are acoustic vibrations pitched beyond what a human ear can hear.

clue.text: Masked Los Angeles advert in a crazy fashion

indicators.note: something done crazily is done in a wild disorder, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: LA is the usual abbreviation for Los Angeles
used letter for letter

explanation.surface: A wild, disguised advertising campaign in Hollywood.
explanation.walkthrough: LARVATED is a rare word, from Latin larva, which once meant a mask.
explanation.definitionFit: Larvated means wearing a mask or concealed, from the Latin larva, a ghost or mask.

clue.text: Removed my robe during early stage of development

indicators.note: removed is read as re-moved, moved about again, so the letters change places

blocks.note: both words used letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone took off their gown at the start of a project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Removed' reads as taking clothes off; it is re-moved, the letters moved around.
explanation.definitionFit: An embryo is an organism in its first phase of growth, before it becomes a fetus.

clue.text: Way before exploitation to remove one's clothes

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street
a rip-off is an act of cheating someone

explanation.surface: A street scam ends with somebody undressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' just places the street ahead of the swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip off is to take off all your garments, which is undressing.

clue.text: Glen leaving town in Fife for Speyside village

indicators.note: leaving means going away, so that word departs from the town's name

blocks.note: the word itself, which is removed
Glenrothes is a new town in Fife, Scotland

explanation.surface: Someone called Glen moves from Fife to a village on the River Spey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glen' looks like a person's name or a valley, but it is the first part of GLENROTHES, a Fife town; what remains is a Speyside village known for its whisky distilleries.
explanation.definitionFit: Rothes is a small town in Moray on the River Spey, in the whisky-making region called Speyside.

clue.text: Slim continental friend accepted vitamin

indicators.note: something that has accepted another has taken it in, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: slim and thin both mean slender
ami is French for friend; continental means from mainland Europe

explanation.surface: A slender European friend took a vitamin supplement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Continental' tells you to use a European language, here French.
explanation.definitionFit: Thiamin is vitamin B1, found in whole grains and needed for energy metabolism.

clue.text: Features cool spacecraft

blocks.note: a film that features an actor stars them
hip is slang for fashionable

explanation.surface: A trendy rocket with distinctive design details.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Features' reads as a noun, but it is the verb: a film features or STARS an actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A starship is a vessel for travelling between stars, so a kind of craft for space.

clue.text: Striking lucky chance with sound of a bell

blocks.note: a hit can be a stroke of luck or success
ting is the light ringing note of a small bell

explanation.surface: A clock's chime strikes by chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' sits with the bell to suggest a clock striking; it is the definition, meaning hitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Striking and hitting both mean delivering a blow to something.

clue.text: Mollusc, one losing its footing with one that sticks to rocks

blocks.note: one who slips loses their footing
a limpet is a shellfish that clings tightly to rocks

explanation.surface: A sea creature that loses its grip beside one that clings on.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves are small cryptic definitions, made funnier because a limpet's grip is its famous foot.
explanation.definitionFit: The slipper limpet is a sea snail whose shell looks like a slipper; it is a gastropod.

clue.text: Arguments soundly stimulate

indicators.note: soundly here means by sound, so the word is the one heard rather than seen

blocks.note: rows, rhyming with cows, are noisy quarrels

explanation.surface: Rows that are well-made stir people up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly' reads as thoroughly; it means in sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse is to stir up or awaken, so it means stimulating someone to act.

clue.text: President thanks newspaper

blocks.note: ta is informal British for thanks
the FT is the Financial Times

explanation.surface: A head of state thanks a paper for its coverage.
explanation.walkthrough: The FT is the Financial Times, a British daily paper printed on pink paper.
explanation.definitionFit: William Howard Taft was the 27th US president, holding office from 1909 to 1913.

clue.text: Wee Italian

definitions.note: the phrase is Italian; 'Italian' qualifies rather than defines on its own

blocks.note: children's euphemism: a wee is 'number one'
the Italian phrase for number one

explanation.walkthrough: 'Wee' looks like Scots for small, so a small Italian; but to wee is to do a 'number one', and this is the Italian for that phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Numero uno is Italian for number one, and number one is nursery slang for urinating.

clue.text: Lamb went round the bend for this lady

indicators.note: going round something means encircling it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: Elia was the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb
a zigzag bend shaped like the letter Z

explanation.surface: A gentle sheep that went mad over a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lamb' looks like the animal; it is the writer Charles Lamb, who signed his essays ELIA. 'Round the bend' means mad, but here it splits into a container and Z.
explanation.definitionFit: Eliza is a woman's first name, so it names a lady, linking to the other ladies in the puzzle.

clue.text: Garcon kept holding his nose

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the run of words keeps the target inside

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: A French waiter pinches his nose, perhaps at a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Conk is British slang for the nose, so 'his nose' becomes his conk.

clue.text: Nobody else instructed one to be this

definitions.text: Nobody else instructed one to be this

blocks.note: surface reading: a person given orders by no one, perhaps a free agent
setter's reading: instructed in the sense of taught, by no teacher but oneself

explanation.walkthrough: 'Instructed' reads as ordered; take it as educated, and the person with no other teacher learned alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone self-taught gained knowledge without a teacher, so no other person schooled them.
